question:
Which of the following statements about oxidation and reduction are correct?

I. A substance is said to be oxidised if it gains oxygen or loses hydrogen.

II. A substance is reduced if it loses oxygen or gains hydrogen.

III. In every redox reaction, both oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously.
solution_text:
The correct answer is I, II, and III.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Oxidation is the gain of oxygen or the loss of hydrogen by a substance; reduction is the loss of oxygen or the gain of hydrogen. (ऑक्सीकरण एवं अपचयन — ऑक्सीजन/हाइड्रोजन का आदान-प्रदान)

 

• In electronic terms, oxidation is loss of electrons and reduction is gain of electrons — this is the more general definition used at higher levels.

 

• A reaction in which oxidation and reduction happen together is called a redox reaction; the two processes can never occur alone — the substance that gets oxidised gives electrons/hydrogen to the substance that gets reduced.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Oxidising agent: itself gets reduced while oxidising another substance (e.g., O₂, KMnO₄, K₂Cr₂O₇).

 

• Reducing agent: itself gets oxidised while reducing another substance (e.g., H₂, C, CO, H₂S).

 

• Rusting of iron, respiration in living beings and combustion of fuels are everyday examples of oxidation reactions.

 

NOTE

 

• I and II only (Option A): Leaves out statement III, which is also a correct, standard fact about redox reactions.

 

• I and III only (Option B): Leaves out statement II, which correctly defines reduction.

 

• II and III only (Option C): Leaves out statement I, which correctly defines oxidation.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

A) The formula unit mass of CaCl2 is 111 u.

B) The formula unit mass is calculated in the same manner as we calculate the molecular mass.

C) The formula unit mass is calculated in a manner that is different to how we calculate the molecular mass.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only A and B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Formula unit mass of CaCl₂ = Ca (40 u) + 2 × Cl (35.5 u) = 40 + 71 = 111 u, so statement A is correct. (सूत्र इकाई द्रव्यमान — CaCl₂ = 111 u)

 

• The formula unit mass of an ionic compound is obtained by adding up the atomic masses of all the atoms present in its formula unit — this is exactly the same procedure used to calculate the molecular mass of a molecular compound. So statement B is correct, and consequently statement C (which claims the procedure is different) is incorrect.

 

• The term "formula unit mass" is preferred for ionic compounds (like NaCl, CaCl₂) because they don't exist as discrete molecules, only as a repeating lattice of ions; "molecular mass" is used for compounds that exist as true molecules (like H₂O, CO₂).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Molecular mass = sum of the atomic masses of all atoms in one molecule of a substance, expressed in atomic mass units (u) or amu.

 

• Molar mass is the mass (in grams) of one mole of a substance — numerically equal to its atomic/molecular/formula unit mass, but expressed in g/mol.

 

• The concept of atomic mass unit (u) is defined by taking 1/12th the mass of one atom of Carbon-12 as the standard unit.

 

NOTE

 

• Only A (Option B): Wrongly excludes statement B, which is also a true, standard fact about formula unit mass calculation.

 

• Only B and C (Option C): Wrongly includes C, since statement C directly contradicts the true statement B.

 

• Only D (Option D): There is no valid basis for this choice, since statement C (on which it would depend) is false.

question: If 0.2 A current flows through a wire when the potential difference across it is 2 V, what is the resistance of the wire?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10 Ω.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• By Ohm's Law, V = IR, so Resistance R = V ÷ I. (ओम का नियम — R = V/I)

 

• Here V = 2 V and I = 0.2 A, so R = 2 ÷ 0.2 = 10 Ω.

 

• Ohm's law holds true only for ohmic conductors at constant physical conditions (like temperature); the V–I graph for such conductors is a straight line through the origin.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• SI unit of resistance is the ohm (Ω); 1 Ω is the resistance of a conductor across which a potential difference of 1 V drives a current of 1 A.

 

• Resistance of a conductor: R = ρl/A, where ρ is resistivity, l is length and A is area of cross-section — resistance increases with length and decreases with area.

 

• Resistivity depends only on the material and temperature of the conductor, not on its shape or size.

 

NOTE

 

• 1 Ω (Option B) and 4 Ω (Option C): Would result from mistakenly dividing or multiplying the given values incorrectly (e.g., I ÷ V or V × I) instead of applying R = V/I.

 

• Option D: Not a valid resistance for the given values; only R = 10 Ω satisfies Ohm's law here.

question: Which of the following is the fluid content inside the plasma membrane?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cytoplasm.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The cytoplasm is the jelly-like fluid content enclosed within the plasma membrane of a cell, in which all cell organelles are suspended. (कोशिका द्रव्य — प्लाज्मा झिल्ली के भीतर तरल पदार्थ)

 

• It consists mainly of water along with dissolved salts, proteins, carbohydrates and other biomolecules, and is the site of many metabolic reactions like glycolysis.

 

• The plasma membrane (cell membrane) is a selectively permeable membrane made of a lipid bilayer with embedded proteins; it controls the entry and exit of substances into and out of the cell.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ribosomes are tiny granular organelles (found free in the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum) that are the site of protein synthesis.

 

• The nuclear membrane is a double-layered membrane that separates the nucleus from the cytoplasm and has pores for exchange of material.

 

• The cell wall is a rigid, non-living outer covering found in plant cells, fungi and bacteria, made mainly of cellulose in plants — it is absent in animal cells.

 

NOTE

 

• Ribosomes (Option A): Cell organelles suspended in the cytoplasm, not the fluid itself.

 

• Nuclear membrane (Option B): Encloses the nucleus, a separate structure from the plasma membrane.

 

• Cell wall (Option D): A rigid outer boundary present only in certain cells (plants, fungi, bacteria), located outside the plasma membrane.

question: Which of the following does NOT involve oxidation reaction?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dissolution of salt in water.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dissolving common salt (NaCl) in water is a physical change, not a chemical reaction — the Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions merely get surrounded by water molecules and separate; no new substance is formed and no oxidation/reduction occurs. (लवण का जल में घुलना — भौतिक परिवर्तन)

 

• All the other three options involve genuine chemical oxidation: burning of wood and rusting of iron are both reactions with atmospheric oxygen; electrolysis of water produces O₂ gas at the anode, where oxidation (loss of electrons by O²⁻ ions/water molecules) takes place.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rusting is the oxidation of iron in the presence of moisture and oxygen to form hydrated iron(III) oxide (Fe₂O₃·xH₂O); it can be prevented by painting, galvanising or oiling.

 

• Combustion (burning) is a rapid oxidation reaction that releases heat and light; wood burning produces CO₂ and water vapour along with ash.

 

• In electrolysis of water, hydrogen gas is liberated at the cathode (reduction) and oxygen gas at the anode (oxidation), in a 2:1 volume ratio (H₂:O₂).

 

NOTE

 

• Electrolysis of water (Option A): Involves oxidation of water/oxide ions at the anode to release O₂ gas.

 

• Burning of wood (Option C): A combustion reaction — wood's carbon and hydrogen combine with atmospheric oxygen (oxidation).

 

• Rusting of iron (Option D): A slow oxidation of iron metal by oxygen and moisture over time.

question: What happens when an unbalanced force acts on an object?
option_1: The object remains at rest permanently
option_2: The object always moves in a circular path
option_3: The object moves without any acceleration
option_4: There is a change in the object's speed or direction of motion
solution_text:
The correct answer is There is a change in the object's speed or direction of motion.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, an unbalanced (net) force acting on a body produces acceleration in it, which means it changes the body's speed and/or direction of motion. (असंतुलित बल — गति में परिवर्तन)

 

• A balanced force (net force = zero) does not change the state of motion — a body at rest stays at rest, and a moving body continues at the same speed in the same direction (Newton's First Law / law of inertia).

 

• Mathematically, F = ma; if F (net/unbalanced force) is non-zero, acceleration 'a' must also be non-zero, causing a change in velocity (which includes speed and/or direction).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Newton's First Law (Law of Inertia): A body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by an unbalanced (external) force.

 

• Newton's Second Law: Rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied unbalanced force, and takes place in the direction of the force (F = ma).

 

• Newton's Third Law: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.

 

NOTE

 

• The object remains at rest permanently (Option A): True only if the object was already at rest AND the net force stays zero — an unbalanced force would actually set it in motion.

 

• The object always moves in a circular path (Option B): Only true for a special case (a constant force perpendicular to velocity, like centripetal force); not true in general.

 

• The object moves without any acceleration (Option C): Contradicts Newton's Second Law — an unbalanced force always produces acceleration.

question: The anion formed by which of the following non-metals reacts with Ca2+ ion to form a stable ionic compound?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Oxygen.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Oxygen gains 2 electrons to attain the stable noble gas configuration, forming the oxide ion (O²⁻). (ऑक्सीजन — O²⁻ आयन)

 

• Since Ca²⁺ also carries a charge of +2, it combines with O²⁻ in a simple 1:1 ratio to form the electrically neutral, stable ionic compound calcium oxide (CaO).

 

• Ionic compounds form when a metal loses electrons (forming a cation, here Ca → Ca²⁺ + 2e⁻) and a non-metal gains electrons (forming an anion) — the resulting oppositely charged ions attract each other via strong electrostatic (ionic) bonds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ionic (electrovalent) bonds are formed by the complete transfer of electrons from a metal to a non-metal, and are typically strong, giving ionic compounds high melting/boiling points.

 

• Properties of ionic compounds: hard and brittle solids, high melting and boiling points, generally soluble in water, and conduct electricity only in the molten or aqueous state (not in solid state).

 

• Calcium (Group 2, atomic number 20) always forms a +2 cation by losing its two valence electrons.

 

NOTE

 

• Boron (Option B): A metalloid that typically forms covalent bonds rather than a simple stable anion; it does not readily form a Ca-boride via simple ionic bonding in this way.

 

• Carbon (Option C): Has 4 valence electrons and generally forms covalent bonds by sharing electrons, not simple ionic anions like O²⁻.

 

• Nitrogen (Option D): Forms the N³⁻ ion, which combines with Ca²⁺ in a 3:2 ratio (Ca₃N₂) — not as simple/stable a 1:1 pairing as CaO.

question: Which of the following is an example of natural ecosystem?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Forests.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A forest is a classic example of a natural ecosystem — it develops and sustains itself entirely through natural processes, without ongoing human management, and contains a self-sufficient community of plants, animals and microorganisms interacting with their physical environment. (वन — प्राकृतिक पारितंत्र)

 

• Artificial (man-made) ecosystems, by contrast, are created and maintained by human beings and require continuous human intervention/inputs to survive.

 

• Other natural ecosystems include ponds, lakes, rivers, grasslands, deserts and oceans.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• An ecosystem = biotic community (living organisms) + abiotic environment (air, water, soil, sunlight), interacting as a functional unit.

 

• Ecosystems are broadly classified into terrestrial (forest, grassland, desert) and aquatic (pond, lake, ocean, estuary) types.

 

• A food chain within an ecosystem shows the transfer of energy from producers to various levels of consumers; a food web is an interconnected network of multiple food chains.

 

NOTE

 

• Fish aquarium (Option A): An artificial, human-maintained mini-ecosystem requiring regular feeding, filtration and monitoring.

 

• Hydroponics (Option B): A man-made technique of growing plants in nutrient solution without soil, entirely dependent on human management.

 

• Kitchen garden (Option C): A small, human-cultivated patch for growing vegetables/herbs — an artificial ecosystem.

question: Which of the following is a psychological change associated with sexual maturity?
option_2: Desire of independence and mood swings
solution_text:
The correct answer is Desire of independence and mood swings.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• During adolescence/puberty, along with physical changes, there occur significant psychological (mental/emotional) changes, such as a growing desire for independence, mood swings, increased self-consciousness and interest in the opposite sex. (मनोवैज्ञानिक परिवर्तन — किशोरावस्था)

 

• These emotional changes are triggered by the surge of sex hormones — testosterone in boys and oestrogen in girls — during puberty, alongside the physical (somatic) changes.

 

• Puberty is the period during adolescence when a person becomes capable of sexual reproduction, typically beginning between the ages of 11 and 19.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Physical changes in puberty include growth of body/facial hair, voice change (in boys), development of secondary sexual characteristics, and growth spurts — these are physiological, not psychological.

 

• Secondary sexual characters in boys: facial hair, broadening of shoulders, deepening of voice. In girls: development of breasts, widening of hips, onset of menstruation.

 

• The hypothalamus and pituitary gland regulate the release of sex hormones that trigger puberty.

 

NOTE

 

• Hair growth on skin (Option A): A physical (somatic) change of puberty, not a psychological one.

 

• Increased physical activity (Option C): Relates to physical energy/behaviour, not classified as a core psychological change of sexual maturity.

 

• Development of brain (Option D): Brain development is a separate, ongoing biological process, not specifically a hallmark psychological change of sexual maturity.

question: Which of the following products is formed on complete combustion of hydrocarbons?
solution_text:
The correct answer is CO₂ and water.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon occurs when there is a sufficient (excess) supply of oxygen, producing carbon dioxide (CO₂) and water (H₂O), along with the release of heat and light. (पूर्ण दहन — CO₂ और जल)

 

• Example: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O + heat/light (complete combustion of methane).

 

• Incomplete combustion, which occurs with a limited/insufficient supply of oxygen, produces carbon monoxide (CO) and/or soot (unburnt carbon) instead of CO₂.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Carbon monoxide (CO) is a poisonous, colourless, odourless gas produced by incomplete combustion — it binds with haemoglobin more strongly than oxygen, which can be fatal.

 

• A blue flame (as in an LPG stove burning properly) indicates complete combustion; a yellow, sooty flame indicates incomplete combustion.

 

• Combustion of hydrocarbons is a major source of greenhouse gas (CO₂) emissions, contributing to global warming.

 

NOTE

 

• Methane and hydrogen (Option A) and Methane and oxygen (Option B): Methane is itself the hydrocarbon being burnt (the reactant, not the product); these are not combustion products.

 

• CO and water (Option D): These are the products of incomplete combustion (insufficient oxygen), not complete combustion.

question: Which of the following statements about nervous tissue is correct?
option_1: Nervous tissue is responsible for voluntary movement and is attached to bones.
option_2: Nervous tissue is composed of epithelial cells that form protective layers.
option_3: Nervous tissue consists of neurons and is found in the brain, spinal cord and nerves
option_4: Nervous tissue is made up of muscle fibres responsible for movement.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nervous tissue consists of neurons and is found in the brain, spinal cord and nerves.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nervous tissue is made up of specialised cells called neurons (nerve cells), which are the structural and functional unit of the nervous system, and is found in the brain, spinal cord and nerves. (तंत्रिका ऊतक — न्यूरॉन)

 

• Neurons are highly specialised to receive stimuli and conduct nerve impulses rapidly from one part of the body to another, enabling communication and coordination.

 

• A typical neuron has three parts: the cell body (cyton), dendrites (which receive impulses) and a long axon (which transmits impulses away from the cell body).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Muscular tissue (not nervous tissue) is responsible for voluntary and involuntary movement, and is attached to bones (skeletal muscle) to enable movement.

 

• Epithelial tissue forms protective covering/lining layers of the body (skin, lining of gut, blood vessels, etc.), and is not related to the nervous system.

 

• The synapse is the junction between two neurons where a nerve impulse passes from one neuron to the next, usually via chemical messengers called neurotransmitters.

 

NOTE

 

• Option A describes a function of muscular tissue, not nervous tissue.

 

• Option B describes epithelial tissue, which forms protective/lining layers made of epithelial cells, not nervous tissue.

 

• Option D describes muscular tissue, which is made of muscle fibres and enables movement, not nervous tissue.

question: Why is the gravitational force considered a weak force in everyday terrestrial interactions, such as between you and a friend sitting nearby?
option_1: Because the force is only experienced when the objects are in free fall.
option_2: Because the distance between the objects is negligibly small.
option_3: Because the mass of human objects is much greater than the Earth's mass.
option_4: Because the force is only significant when large masses (like planets or celestial bodies) are involved.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Because the force is only significant when large masses (like planets or celestial bodies) are involved.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• By Newton's law of gravitation, F = Gm₁m₂/r², the gravitational force is directly proportional to the product of the two masses involved. (गुरुत्वाकर्षण बल — द्रव्यमान के अनुक्रमानुपाती)

 

• Since the gravitational constant G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m²/kg² is extremely small, and everyday objects (like people) have comparatively tiny masses, the resulting gravitational force between them is too small to be noticed.

 

• This force becomes significant/noticeable only when at least one of the interacting masses is very large, such as a planet, star, or celestial body — which is why we readily feel the Earth's gravitational pull but not that of a nearby person.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gravitational force is the weakest of the four fundamental forces of nature (the other three being electromagnetic force, strong nuclear force and weak nuclear force), yet it dominates at large (astronomical) scales because it is always attractive and has infinite range.

 

• Acceleration due to gravity (g) on Earth's surface is about 9.8 m/s², derived from g = GM/R², where M and R are Earth's mass and radius.

 

• Gravitational force keeps planets in orbit around the Sun, the Moon in orbit around the Earth, and is responsible for tides, weight of objects, and free fall.

 

NOTE

 

• Free fall (Option A): Free fall is a consequence of gravity acting alone (without other resisting forces like air resistance), not the condition under which gravity is "experienced" — gravity acts at all times, not only during free fall.

 

• Negligible distance (Option B): A smaller distance would actually make gravitational force stronger (F ∝ 1/r²), not explain why it's weak.

 

• Human mass greater than Earth's (Option C): Factually false — Earth's mass (~5.97 × 10²⁴ kg) is vastly greater than any human's mass.

question: In a concave mirror, a ray of light directed towards the principal focus after reflection:
option_2: Passes through the center of curvature
option_4: Becomes parallel to the principal axis
solution_text:
The correct answer is Becomes parallel to the principal axis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• This is the reverse case of the standard ray-tracing rule for concave mirrors: a ray travelling towards the principal focus (F) strikes the mirror and, after reflection, travels parallel to the principal axis. (अवतल दर्पण — फोकस की ओर आने वाली किरण परावर्तन के बाद अक्ष के समानांतर)

 

• This follows directly from the principle of reversibility of light — since a ray parallel to the axis reflects and passes through F, a ray travelling (in the reverse direction) towards F must reflect and become parallel to the axis.

 

• This rule is one of the standard ray diagrams used to locate images formed by concave mirrors.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Standard ray rules for concave mirrors: (i) A ray parallel to the principal axis, after reflection, passes through the focus. (ii) A ray passing through the focus, after reflection, becomes parallel to the axis. (iii) A ray passing through the centre of curvature (C), after reflection, retraces its own path (since it strikes the mirror normally). (iv) A ray striking the pole is reflected obeying the laws of reflection (equal angles with the axis).

 

• The focal length (f) of a spherical mirror is related to its radius of curvature (R) by f = R/2.

 

• A concave mirror is a converging mirror and can form both real and virtual images depending on the object's position, while a convex mirror always forms a virtual, diminished image.

 

NOTE

 

• Diverges away from the axis (Option A): Incorrect — the reflected ray converges to become parallel to the axis, it does not diverge.

 

• Passes through the centre of curvature (Option B): This describes what happens to a ray that is already directed towards/from the centre of curvature, not one directed towards the focus.

 

• Retraces its path (Option C): This is the behaviour of a ray directed towards the centre of curvature, since it hits the mirror perpendicularly (along the normal), not a ray aimed at the focus.

question: Through the phenomenon of biological magnification, which of the following has the maximum concentration of pesticides in them?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Snake.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Biological magnification (biomagnification) is the phenomenon in which the concentration of harmful, non-biodegradable chemicals (like pesticides such as DDT) increases at each successive trophic level of a food chain. (जैव आवर्धन — खाद्य श्रृंखला में उच्च पोषी स्तर पर प्रदूषक का अधिकतम सांद्रण)

 

• The food chain here is: Grass (producer) → Grasshopper (primary consumer) → Frog (secondary consumer) → Snake (tertiary/top consumer).

 

• Since the snake occupies the highest (topmost) trophic level in this chain, pesticide residues accumulated by all the organisms below it get concentrated further in its body, giving it the maximum concentration of pesticide.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• DDT (Dichloro-Diphenyl-Trichloroethane) is a classic example of a non-biodegradable pesticide that undergoes biomagnification; it was widely used as an insecticide but is now banned/restricted in many countries because of this hazard.

 

• Biomagnification is a major reason why top predators (like birds of prey, big cats, or humans) are most severely affected by persistent chemical pollutants, even though they may never directly consume the chemical.

 

• Trophic level: each successive step in the transfer of food/energy in a food chain — producers form the first trophic level, and energy decreases (roughly by 90%, per the 10% law) while toxin concentration increases as we move up.

 

NOTE

 

• Grasshopper (Option A): A primary consumer, low in the food chain — receives some pesticide from grass but far less than the snake.

 

• Grass (Option B): The producer, the very first trophic level, where pesticide concentration is lowest (this is where the contamination first enters the food chain, typically in trace amounts).

 

• Frog (Option D): A secondary consumer, positioned below the snake in this food chain, so it has less concentrated pesticide than the snake, though more than the grasshopper.

question: A compass needle placed near a current-carrying conductor shows deflection because:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Current produces magnetic field.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• This deflection was first observed by Hans Christian Oersted (1820), who found that a current-carrying conductor produces a magnetic field around it, which exerts a force on the magnetic needle of a nearby compass, causing it to deflect. (धारावाही चालक — चुंबकीय क्षेत्र उत्पन्न करता है)

 

• This experiment established the important link between electricity and magnetism, forming the foundation of the field of electromagnetism.

 

• The direction of the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying conductor is given by the Right-Hand Thumb Rule: if the thumb points in the direction of current flow, the curled fingers show the direction of the magnetic field lines.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The strength of the magnetic field around a straight conductor increases with an increase in current and decreases with increasing distance from the conductor.

 

• A solenoid (a coil of many circular turns of wire) carrying current produces a magnetic field pattern similar to that of a bar magnet, and is used to make electromagnets.

 

• This principle (current → magnetic field) is the basis of devices like the electric motor, galvanometer and electromagnet.

 

NOTE

 

• Current produces heat (Option A): True (Joule heating, H = I²Rt), but heat does not cause a compass needle to deflect.

 

• Current produces electric field (Option C): A stationary/moving charge does produce an electric field, but it is the associated magnetic field of the moving charges (current) that specifically deflects a compass needle.

 

• Current produces sound (Option D): Not a general property of current flow; irrelevant to the compass deflection phenomenon.

question: Which of the following statements is correct about reproduction in plants?
option_1: Gametes can alone produce new offspring.
option_2: Spores can alone produce new offspring.
option_3: Spores need fusion with another spore to produce new offspring.
option_4: Spores are produced only during sexual reproduction.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Spores can alone produce new offspring.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Spores are asexual reproductive structures (usually single-celled, often with a protective covering) that can germinate directly into a new individual on their own, without needing to fuse with another cell — this is a hallmark feature of asexual reproduction. (बीजाणु — अलैंगिक जनन)

 

• Common spore-forming organisms include fungi (like Rhizopus/bread mould), mosses and ferns.

 

• In contrast, gametes (sex cells, like the male and female reproductive cells) cannot develop into a new organism alone — they must fuse (fertilise) with a gamete of the opposite sex to form a zygote, which then develops into a new offspring; this is sexual reproduction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Asexual reproduction methods in plants also include vegetative propagation (like potato tubers, ginger rhizomes) and budding.

 

• Sexual reproduction in flowering plants involves fusion of male gametes (from pollen) with the female gamete (egg cell in the ovule), a process called fertilisation, following pollination.

 

• Spores are typically produced through mitosis (in many fungi/mosses) or via specialised sporangia, and are usually lightweight for easy dispersal by wind or water.

 

NOTE

 

• Gametes can alone produce new offspring (Option A): Incorrect — gametes must fuse with an opposite gamete (fertilisation) to form offspring; they cannot develop alone.

 

• Spores need fusion with another spore (Option C): Incorrect — this describes gametes, not spores; spores germinate independently.

 

• Spores are produced only during sexual reproduction (Option D): Incorrect — spores are primarily associated with asexual reproduction, not sexual reproduction.

question: What is the minimum time gap needed between the original sound and its echo for us to hear a clear echo?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 0.1 seconds.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sensation of any sound heard by the human ear persists in the brain for about 0.1 second. (प्रतिध्वनि — न्यूनतम समय अंतराल 0.1 सेकंड)

 

• For an echo to be heard as a distinct, separate sound (rather than blending with the original sound), the reflected sound must reach the listener's ear at least 0.1 second after the original sound.

 

• Using this, the minimum distance of the reflecting surface from the source (for a clear echo) can be calculated: taking the speed of sound in air as about 344 m/s, minimum distance = (344 × 0.1) ÷ 2 = 17.2 metres (divided by 2 because sound travels to the obstacle and back).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option Bᅟ(printed in this booklet as "B).1 seconds", representing 0.1 seconds).

 

Additional Information

 

• Reverberation is the persistence of sound in a large hall due to multiple, closely-spaced reflections — it is different from a distinct echo, and is minimised using sound-absorbent materials.

 

• Applications based on reflection/echo of sound include SONAR (used to determine the depth of the sea or detect underwater objects) and ultrasound imaging.

 

• The audible range of sound for human beings is 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz; sound below 20 Hz is infrasonic and above 20,000 Hz is ultrasonic.

 

NOTE

 

• 1 second (Option A): Far longer than the minimum gap actually required to perceive a distinct echo.

 

• Option C (printed as "C).01 seconds", i.e. 0.01 seconds): Too short — the human ear cannot resolve two sounds that close together as separate; they would blend into one.

 

• 10 seconds (Option D): An unrealistically long gap; not the minimum requirement.

question: What is the primary function of epithelial tissue?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Protection.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The primary function of epithelial tissue is protection — it covers the outer surface of the body (skin) and lines internal organs and cavities, forming a protective barrier against mechanical injury, pathogens, and desiccation (water loss). (उपकला ऊतक — रक्षा)

 

• Epithelial cells are tightly packed with little to no intercellular space, forming continuous, unbroken sheets that act as effective barriers.

 

• Besides protection, some epithelial tissues are also specialised for absorption (e.g., in the intestine), secretion (glandular epithelium) and sensation (e.g., in the tongue, nose).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Types of epithelial tissue include squamous (flat cells, e.g., skin, lining of blood vessels), cuboidal (e.g., in kidney tubules), columnar (e.g., in the intestine) and ciliated epithelium (e.g., lining of the respiratory tract, helps move mucus).

 

• Epithelial tissue rests on a basement membrane that separates it from the underlying connective tissue.

 

• The four basic types of animal tissue are: epithelial, connective, muscular and nervous tissue.

 

NOTE

 

• Support (Option B): This is a key function of connective tissue (e.g., bone, cartilage), not epithelial tissue.

 

• Control (Option C): This is primarily a function of nervous tissue, which coordinates and controls body activities.

 

• Movement (Option D): This is primarily a function of muscular tissue, which contracts to cause movement.

question: Select the correct example of a crystalline solid.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both sugar and salt.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Crystalline solids are those whose constituent particles (atoms, ions or molecules) are arranged in a highly ordered, repeating three-dimensional pattern, giving them a definite geometric shape, sharp melting point, and flat faces. (क्रिस्टलीय ठोस — निश्चित ज्यामितीय आकार)

 

• Both sugar (sucrose) and common salt (sodium chloride) are classic examples of crystalline solids, each possessing a definite, ordered crystal structure and a sharp melting point.

 

• Sand, by contrast, is generally treated at this level as lacking the single, well-ordered structure of a true crystal (its particles do not show the same long-range order), so it does not qualify as a straightforward crystalline solid example here.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Amorphous solids (like glass, rubber and plastic) lack a regular/ordered internal arrangement of particles; they have irregular shapes and melt over a range of temperatures rather than at one sharp point.

 

• On heating, a crystalline solid melts sharply at a fixed temperature, while an amorphous solid gradually softens over a range of temperatures (this is used to distinguish the two).

 

• Common examples of crystalline solids (besides sugar and salt): diamond, quartz, ice, copper sulphate crystals (blue vitriol).

 

NOTE

 

• Only sand (Option A): Incomplete/incorrect — sand alone is not treated as the (best) crystalline example here; salt and sugar are.

 

• Only salt (Option B): Incomplete — leaves out sugar, which is equally a valid crystalline solid.

 

• All salt, sugar and sand (Option D): Incorrect — wrongly includes sand along with the two genuine crystalline examples.

question: If a constant force of 10 N moves an object 5 m in the same direction as the force, the work done is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 50 J.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Work done (W) = Force (F) × displacement (s) × cos θ, where θ is the angle between the force and the direction of displacement. (कार्य = बल × विस्थापन)

 

• Since the force and displacement here are in the same direction, θ = 0° and cos 0° = 1, so W = F × s.

 

• W = 10 N × 5 m = 50 J (joules).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• SI unit of work is the joule (J); 1 joule of work is done when a force of 1 newton displaces an object by 1 metre in the direction of the force.

 

• If the force and displacement are perpendicular (θ = 90°), the work done is zero (e.g., a person carrying a load and walking horizontally does zero work against gravity in the direction of motion).

 

• Work-energy theorem: the net work done on an object equals the change in its kinetic energy.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 J, 5 J, 15 J (Options A, B, C): Would arise from incorrect operations (e.g., dividing F by s, or adding/subtracting F and s) instead of correctly multiplying force by displacement.

question: Which of the following is a T-shaped intra-uterine contraceptive device that offers long-term (multi-year) birth control?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Copper-T.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Copper-T is a small, T-shaped intra-uterine device (IUD) made of plastic and wound with copper wire, which is inserted into the uterus by a doctor to prevent pregnancy. (कॉपर-टी — गर्भाशय में रखा जाने वाला गर्भनिरोधक उपकरण)

 

• It works mainly by releasing copper ions that are toxic to sperm and interfere with fertilisation/implantation, and it provides effective contraception for several years (typically 5–10 years) once inserted, without requiring daily attention.

 

• It is a widely used, reversible method of long-acting, mechanical/chemical barrier contraception for women.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Contraceptive methods are broadly classified as: barrier methods (condom, diaphragm, cervical cap), chemical methods (spermicidal creams/foams), hormonal methods (oral pills, injectables, implants), IUDs (like Copper-T), and surgical methods (vasectomy in males, tubectomy in females).

 

• Oral contraceptive pills work by altering hormonal balance to prevent ovulation, and must be taken regularly (typically daily).

 

• Condoms are barrier devices that also help prevent sexually transmitted infections (STIs), in addition to preventing pregnancy.

 

NOTE

 

• Birth control pill (Option B): A hormonal method taken orally, requiring regular (usually daily) intake — not a physical device placed in the uterus.

 

• Diaphragm (Option C): A barrier method — a dome-shaped device placed in the vagina before intercourse to block sperm; it must be inserted each time, unlike a long-term IUD.

 

• Male condom (Option D): A barrier method used by males during each act of intercourse; not a long-term device.

question: The wavering of objects seen through a turbulent hot air stream is an example of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is small-scale atmospheric refraction.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hot air above a heat source (like a flame, a hot road, or a stream of turbulent hot air) is less dense than the surrounding cooler air, and its density/refractive index keeps changing randomly and continuously due to turbulence. (वायुमंडलीय अपवर्तन — तारों का टिमटिमाना, मृगतृष्णा जैसी घटनाएँ)

 

• Light rays passing through these constantly-changing layers of air (of differing optical density) get refracted differently at each instant, causing objects viewed through them to appear to shimmer, waver or flicker — this is called small-scale (or 'local') atmospheric refraction.

 

• This same underlying principle (light bending due to a gradually changing refractive index of air) also explains related phenomena like the twinkling of stars and the mirage effect seen on hot roads/deserts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Twinkling of stars occurs because starlight, before reaching our eyes, passes through the Earth's atmosphere where the refractive index of air keeps changing due to varying temperature/density, causing the apparent position and brightness of the star to fluctuate.

 

• A mirage is an optical illusion (often seen in deserts or on hot roads) caused by the total internal reflection of light due to a gradual change in the refractive index of air layers near a very hot surface.

 

• Advance sunrise / delayed sunset (the Sun becoming visible about 2 minutes before actual sunrise) is another everyday consequence of atmospheric refraction.

 

NOTE

 

• Dispersion of light (Option A): The splitting of white light into its constituent colours (as in a rainbow or via a prism) — unrelated to the wavering effect seen through hot air.

 

• Diffraction in air (Option B): The bending of light around obstacles/edges — not the cause of the shimmering seen through hot air currents.

 

• Internal reflection in air layers (Option C): Relevant to phenomena like mirages specifically (via total internal reflection at a hot surface), but the general "wavering" effect through a turbulent hot air stream is due to continuous refraction, not internal reflection.

question: Which of the following statements is true about mass?
option_1: Mass is a measure of inertia of a body
option_2: Mass and weight are exactly the same
option_3: Mass is a measure of the force acting on a body
option_4: Mass depends on the location of the body
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mass is a measure of inertia of a body.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mass is defined as the measure of the inertia of a body — that is, its inherent tendency to resist any change in its state of rest or motion. (द्रव्यमान — जड़त्व का मापन)

 

• The greater the mass of an object, the greater its inertia, meaning it is harder to accelerate/decelerate or change its direction of motion.

 

• Mass is a scalar quantity, measured in kilograms (kg) in the SI system, and remains constant regardless of the object's location (Earth, Moon, or outer space).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Weight = mass × acceleration due to gravity (W = mg); it is a vector quantity, measured in newtons (N), and it varies with location because 'g' varies (e.g., weight on the Moon is about 1/6th of that on Earth).

 

• Force = mass × acceleration (Newton's Second Law, F = ma) — mass is one of the two quantities that determine force, not a direct measure of force itself.

 

• Mass can be measured using a beam balance, while weight is measured using a spring balance.

 

NOTE

 

• Mass and weight are exactly the same (Option B): Incorrect — mass is constant and scalar, while weight is variable (depends on gravity) and is a vector (a type of force).

 

• Mass is a measure of the force acting on a body (Option C): Incorrect — this describes weight, not mass; mass is one of the two factors used to calculate force/weight.

 

• Mass depends on the location of the body (Option D): Incorrect — mass remains the same everywhere in the universe; it is weight, not mass, that changes with location.

question: What happens to the inter-particle space when a solid melts into a liquid?
solution_text:
The correct answer is It increases.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When a solid melts into a liquid, the particles absorb heat energy (latent heat of fusion), which increases their kinetic energy, causing them to vibrate more vigorously and move slightly farther apart, thereby increasing the inter-particle space (and reducing the force of attraction between particles). (गलन — कणों के बीच स्थान में वृद्धि)

 

• In the solid state, particles are very tightly packed with minimum inter-particle space and maximum force of attraction, giving solids a definite shape and volume.

 

• In the liquid state, particles are relatively more loosely packed (though still fairly close compared to gases), which is why liquids can flow and take the shape of their container, while still maintaining a nearly fixed volume.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The general order of inter-particle space is: solid < liquid < gas, and correspondingly, the force of attraction between particles is: solid > liquid > gas.

 

• Latent heat of fusion is the heat energy required to change a unit mass of a substance from solid to liquid at its melting point, without any change in temperature.

 

• When a liquid changes into a gas (vaporisation), the inter-particle space increases even further, and the force of attraction becomes negligible.

 

NOTE

 

• It remains the same (Option B): Incorrect — melting is precisely the process where the tightly-packed solid structure breaks down, increasing particle spacing.

 

• It becomes zero (Option C): Incorrect — inter-particle space can never become exactly zero; it merely increases upon melting.

 

• It decreases (Option D): Incorrect — this is the opposite of what happens; inter-particle spacing decreases during freezing (liquid → solid), not melting.

question: (CH3)3-C-CH3 represents the structural formula of which of the following organic compounds?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2,2-dimethyl propane.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The structure (CH₃)₃–C–CH₃ shows a central carbon atom bonded to four CH₃ (methyl) groups in total — three explicitly shown as (CH₃)₃ plus one more –CH₃, giving the formula C(CH₃)₄, commonly known as neopentane. (नियोपेंटेन — 2,2-डाइमेथिल प्रोपेन)

 

• Naming it by IUPAC rules: the longest carbon chain here is a propane chain (3 carbons: C1–C2–C3), with two methyl (CH₃) substituents both attached to the same, middle (2nd) carbon, giving the name 2,2-dimethylpropane.

 

• This compound has the molecular formula C₅H₁₂ and is an isomer of pentane (along with n-pentane and isopentane/2-methylbutane).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Isomers are compounds having the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements; C₅H₁₂ has three isomers: n-pentane, isopentane (2-methylbutane) and neopentane (2,2-dimethylpropane).

 

• IUPAC nomenclature rule: identify the longest continuous carbon chain (parent chain), number it to give substituents the lowest possible locants, and name branches as substituent prefixes (like methyl, ethyl) with their position numbers.

 

• Saturated hydrocarbons with only single C–C bonds are called alkanes, with the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

 

NOTE

 

• 3-methyl butane (Option A): Not a valid/standard IUPAC name for this structure (butane numbering would put a methyl group incorrectly, and this doesn't correspond to the same structure).

 

• 2,3-dimethyl propane (Option B): Invalid name — propane has only 3 carbons, so a substituent position of '3' would be at the terminal carbon, which cannot carry two identical substituent positions like this in a valid structure.

 

• methyl butane (Option C): An incomplete/ambiguous name (missing the locant number for the methyl group's position); it does not correctly describe this particular structure.

question: The sum of three numbers is 2316. If the ratio between the first and second numbers is 16 : 10 and that of between second and third is 6 : 18, then find the difference between the first and the third number.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 579.

 

GIVEN

 

• Sum of three numbers = 2316.

 

• First : Second = 16 : 10 = 8 : 5, and Second : Third = 6 : 18 = 1 : 3.

 

SOLUTION

 

• To combine the two ratios, make the common term (Second) equal: First : Second = 8 : 5, and Second : Third = 1 : 3 = 5 : 15 (multiplying by 5).

 

• Combined ratio, First : Second : Third = 8 : 5 : 15 (total = 28 parts).

 

• Required difference = Third − First = (15 − 8) parts = 7 parts out of 28, i.e. 7/28 = 1/4 of the total sum.

 

• Difference = (1/4) × 2316 = 579.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• You don't need to find each number separately — just compute the required difference's fraction of the total (here 7/28 = 1/4) and multiply directly by the sum.

 

NOTE

 

• Always combine two ratios by equalising their shared (common) term first — here it was the 'Second' number, common to both given ratios.

question: If the difference of the mode and median of a data is 52, then find the difference of the median and mean.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 26.

 

GIVEN

 

• Mode − Median = 52.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Use the empirical relation between mean, median and mode: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

 

• Rearranging: Mode − Median = 2 × Median − 2 × Mean = 2 × (Median − Mean).

 

• So, Median − Mean = (Mode − Median) ÷ 2 = 52 ÷ 2 = 26.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Memorise the empirical formula Mode = 3(Median) − 2(Mean) — it directly links any two of these differences without needing the actual data.

 

NOTE

 

• This relation is an approximation, standard for moderately skewed distributions at this exam level; treat it as a ready formula.

question: If 20% of a number is added to 84, then the result is the same number. 80% of the same number is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 84.

 

GIVEN

 

• 20% of a number, added to 84, gives back the same number.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the number be x. So 84 + 0.2x = x.

 

• 84 = x − 0.2x = 0.8x, i.e. 84 = 80% of x.

 

• But 80% of x is exactly what the question asks for — so the answer is simply 84, directly from the equation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Spot that the equation 84 = 0.8x is itself the statement '84 equals 80% of the number' — no need to solve for x (which works out to 105) at all.

 

NOTE

 

• Read percentage-word-problems carefully; sometimes the final answer is hidden directly inside the given condition.

question: A sum of money was invested at simple interest at a certain rate for 10 years. Had it been invested at a 6% per annum higher rate, it would have fetched ₹5,700 more. Find the principal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. ₹9,500.

 

GIVEN

 

• Time = 10 years; increase in rate = 6% per annum; extra interest earned = ₹5,700.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Extra Simple Interest = (Principal × Extra Rate × Time) ÷ 100.

 

• 5700 = (P × 6 × 10) ÷ 100 = 0.6P.

 

• P = 5700 ÷ 0.6 = ₹9,500.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• The original rate is irrelevant here — only the rate difference matters: Principal = (Extra Interest × 100) ÷ (Rate Difference × Time).

 

NOTE

 

• A very common SI trap: don't try to find the original rate — it cancels out and is not needed to solve the question.

question: In quadrilateral PQRS, the bisectors of ∠R and ∠S meet at the point T (inside the quadrilateral) and ∠STR = 36°. If the ratio of ∠P to ∠Q is 2 : 7, then what is the difference between the measures of ∠Q and ∠P?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 40°.

 

GIVEN

 

• In quadrilateral PQRS, bisectors of ∠R and ∠S meet at T, and ∠STR = 36°.

 

• ∠P : ∠Q = 2 : 7.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Standard result: the angle between the internal bisectors of two angles (R, S) of a quadrilateral equals half the sum of the other two angles: ∠STR = ½(∠P + ∠Q).

 

• So, 36° = ½(∠P + ∠Q) ⟹ ∠P + ∠Q = 72°.

 

• With ratio 2 : 7 (9 parts total): 1 part = 72° ÷ 9 = 8°. So ∠P = 16°, ∠Q = 56°.

 

• Required difference = ∠Q − ∠P = 56° − 16° = 40°.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Memorise: angle between the bisectors of two angles of a quadrilateral = ½ × (sum of the other two angles) — a very handy ready-made formula.

 

NOTE

 

• Don't confuse this with the analogous triangle formula (angle between two internal bisectors = 90° + half the third angle) — the quadrilateral version is different.

question: If a + b = 8 and ab = 12, calculate the value of a² + b².
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 40.

 

GIVEN

 

• a + b = 8, and ab = 12.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Use the identity: a² + b² = (a + b)² − 2ab.

 

• a² + b² = 8² − 2(12) = 64 − 24 = 40.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always use the algebraic identity (a+b)² = a² + 2ab + b² directly — never waste time solving for individual values of a and b when only a combination like a²+b² is asked.

 

NOTE

 

• Quick check: a, b are roots of x² − 8x + 12 = 0, i.e. (x−2)(x−6) = 0, so a = 2, b = 6 (or vice versa); 2² + 6² = 4 + 36 = 40 ✓.

question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 105?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 4515.

 

GIVEN

 

• 105 = 3 × 5 × 7.

 

SOLUTION

 

• A number divisible by 105 must be divisible by 3, 5 AND 7 simultaneously.

 

• Test 4515: digit sum = 4+5+1+5 = 15 (divisible by 3) ✓; ends in 5 (divisible by 5) ✓; 4515 ÷ 7 = 645 exactly (divisible by 7) ✓.

 

• So 4515 is divisible by 105 (4515 = 105 × 43).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Filter fast using the easy tests first (must end in 0 or 5 for divisibility by 5, and digit-sum divisible by 3), then check only the survivors for divisibility by 7.

 

NOTE

 

• Quick check on the rejects: 4525 (digit sum 16, fails 3); 4675 (digit sum 22, fails 3); 4845 (digit sum 21, divisible by 3, ends in 5, but 4845 ÷ 7 = 692.14…, fails 7).

question: Nick, Kevin, and Joe can finish a certain piece of work in 10, 47, and 24 days, respectively. All three of them started the work together. Nick left the work after 2 days and Kevin left just 5 days before the work was completed. Find the total number of days taken for the work to be completed.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 14.4 days.

 

GIVEN

 

• Nick's 1-day work = 1/10; Kevin's 1-day work = 1/47; Joe's 1-day work = 1/24.

 

• Nick worked only the first 2 days; Kevin worked till 5 days before completion; Joe worked the entire duration (till completion).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the total time taken be T days. Nick worked 2 days, Kevin worked (T − 5) days, Joe worked T days.

 

• Total work equation: 2/10 + (T − 5)/47 + T/24 = 1.

 

• 0.2 + (T−5)/47 + T/24 = 1 ⟹ (T−5)/47 + T/24 = 0.8.

 

• Multiplying throughout by LCM(47, 24) = 1128: 24(T − 5) + 47T = 0.8 × 1128 = 902.4.

 

• 24T − 120 + 47T = 902.4 ⟹ 71T = 1022.4 ⟹ T = 1022.4 ÷ 71 = 14.4 days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Set up one single combined work-equation in the unknown total time T, and solve algebraically rather than trial-fitting integers when the numbers aren't 'clean'.

 

NOTE

 

• The options as printed in this booklet have their leading digit(s) hidden behind the option-letter overlay (a recurring printing glitch in this paper — reproduced here exactly as printed); Option C genuinely reads '14.4', which matches the value derived above.

question: The arithmetic mean of the observations 39, 91, 32, 73, 84, 18, 83, 83 and 28 is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 59.

 

GIVEN

 

• 9 observations: 39, 91, 32, 73, 84, 18, 83, 83, 28.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Sum = 39 + 91 + 32 + 73 + 84 + 18 + 83 + 83 + 28 = 531.

 

• Mean = Sum ÷ Count = 531 ÷ 9 = 59.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Use the assumed-mean method: take assumed mean = 80; deviations are −41, +11, −48, −7, +4, −62, +3, +3, −52, which sum to −189; actual mean = 80 + (−189/9) = 80 − 21 = 59.

 

NOTE

 

• When adding many numbers, group them in convenient pairs (e.g., 39+91=130, 84+18=102) to reduce the chance of an arithmetic slip.

question: Walking at 2/7 of his normal speed, Abhijeet is 30 minutes late in reaching his office. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and his office is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 12 minutes.

 

GIVEN

 

• New speed = 2/7 of usual speed; this makes him 30 minutes late.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Since speed and time are inversely proportional (for a fixed distance), New Time : Usual Time = 7 : 2.

 

• Extra time taken = (7/2 − 1) × Usual Time = (5/2) × T = 30 minutes.

 

• T = 30 × 2/5 = 12 minutes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• If speed becomes a/b of normal, extra time = [(b − a)/a] × usual time. Here (7−2)/2 = 5/2 times the usual time = 30 min, so usual time = 30 × 2/5 = 12 min.

 

NOTE

 

• Always invert the speed ratio to get the time ratio — a very common source of error in speed-time-distance problems.

question: The cost of a washing machine is 25% less than the cost of a TV. If the cost of the washing machine increases by 66% and that of the TV decreases by 57%, then what is the percentage change in the total cost of 7 washing machines and 5 TVs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. Increase by 6%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Washing machine (WM) cost is 25% less than TV cost; WM increases by 66%; TV decreases by 57%; find % change in total cost of 7 WMs + 5 TVs.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Assume TV = ₹100, so WM = ₹75 (25% less).

 

• Original total = 7(75) + 5(100) = 525 + 500 = ₹1025.

 

• New WM = 75 × 1.66 = ₹124.5; New TV = 100 × 0.43 = ₹43.

 

• New total = 7(124.5) + 5(43) = 871.5 + 215 = ₹1086.5.

 

• % change = [(1086.5 − 1025)/1025] × 100 = (61.5/1025) × 100 = 6% increase.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always assume convenient round base values (like TV = 100) when only percentages and ratios are given — it avoids working with unknown variables.

 

NOTE

 

• '25% less than TV' means WM = 0.75 × TV (not TV = 0.75 × WM) — a common trap; get the base relation right before proceeding.

question: What is the average speed of a bike, which covers half the distance with a speed of 42 km/hr and the other half with a speed of 84 km/hr?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 56 km/hr.

 

GIVEN

 

• Equal distances covered at 42 km/hr and 84 km/hr.

 

SOLUTION

 

• For two equal distances covered at speeds a and b, average speed = 2ab/(a + b) (the harmonic mean), NOT the simple arithmetic mean.

 

• Average speed = (2 × 42 × 84) / (42 + 84) = 7056 / 126 = 56 km/hr.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For equal distances at two different speeds, average speed = 2ab/(a+b) — memorise this formula; it's tested very frequently.

 

NOTE

 

• The simple average, (42+84)/2 = 63 km/hr (Option B), is a classic wrong-answer trap — average speed must be based on total distance ÷ total time, never a plain average of speeds.

question: Find the value of sin² 45° + cos² 45°.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 1.

 

GIVEN

 

• Find sin² 45° + cos² 45°.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Use the fundamental trigonometric identity: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, true for every value of θ.

 

• So sin² 45° + cos² 45° = 1 directly, without substituting actual values.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 always — don't waste time substituting sin 45° = cos 45° = 1/√2 and squaring, unless asked to verify.

 

NOTE

 

• Verification: sin 45° = cos 45° = 1/√2, so sin²45° = cos²45° = 1/2, and 1/2 + 1/2 = 1 ✓.

question: One pipe can fill a tank in 9 minutes while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 18 minutes. If both the pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, how many minutes will it take to fill one-half of the tank?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 9 minutes.

 

GIVEN

 

• Filling pipe: fills tank in 9 minutes. Emptying pipe: empties a full tank in 18 minutes. Tank starts empty, both pipes opened together.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take tank capacity = LCM(9, 18) = 18 units. Filling pipe's rate = 18/9 = 2 units/min; emptying pipe's rate = 18/18 = 1 unit/min.

 

• Net filling rate (both open) = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/min.

 

• Half tank = 9 units. Time = 9 units ÷ 1 unit/min = 9 minutes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Assume tank capacity = LCM of the given times — it converts all rates into clean whole numbers, avoiding fraction arithmetic.

 

NOTE

 

• Since the tank starts empty and both pipes work together, only the NET rate (fill rate − empty rate) determines how fast the tank fills — don't use the filling pipe's rate alone.

question: Ajay and Shanu together have ₹1,050. If ₹350 is taken from Ajay, he will have the same amount that Shanu had initially. Find the initial ratio of the amounts with Ajay and Shanu.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 2 : 1.

 

GIVEN

 

• Ajay + Shanu = ₹1,050. Ajay − ₹350 = Shanu's (initial) amount.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let Ajay = A, Shanu = S. So A + S = 1050, and A − 350 = S, i.e. A − S = 350.

 

• Adding the two equations: 2A = 1050 + 350 = 1400 ⟹ A = 700. Then S = 1050 − 700 = 350.

 

• Ratio A : S = 700 : 350 = 2 : 1.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Two simple linear equations (a sum and a difference) can be solved instantly by adding/subtracting them — no need for substitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Read the direction of the comparison carefully: 'Ajay will have the same amount Shanu had initially' means A − 350 = S, not S − 350 = A.

question: A product was sold for ₹980, resulting in a loss of ₹150. To earn a profit of ₹270 instead, what should be its revised selling price?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. ₹1,400.

 

GIVEN

 

• Selling price (SP₁) = ₹980, with a loss of ₹150. Desired profit = ₹270.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Since there is a loss: Cost Price (CP) = SP₁ + Loss = 980 + 150 = ₹1,130.

 

• To earn a profit of ₹270: Revised SP = CP + Profit = 1130 + 270 = ₹1,400.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Find CP first using CP = SP + Loss (or CP = SP − Profit), then simply add the new required profit to CP.

 

NOTE

 

• Don't mix up the formula direction: for a LOSS, CP = SP + Loss; for a PROFIT, CP = SP − Profit.

question: The sides of a triangle are 45 cm, 28 cm, and 53 cm. What is its area (in cm²)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 630 cm².

 

GIVEN

 

• Triangle sides: 45 cm, 28 cm, 53 cm.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Test if it's a right triangle: 28² + 45² = 784 + 2025 = 2809 = 53² ✓. So it is right-angled, with the two smaller sides (28, 45) as the legs.

 

• Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 28 × 45 = 630 cm².

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always test a² + b² = c² for the largest side first; if it fits, area = ½ × product of the two smaller sides — this avoids the lengthier Heron's formula.

 

NOTE

 

• 28-45-53 is a valid (if less common) Pythagorean triplet — worth recognising quickly in exams.

question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 6?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 7132950.

 

GIVEN

 

• Test each number for divisibility by 6.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Divisible by 6 ⟺ divisible by both 2 (even) AND 3 (digit sum divisible by 3).

 

• 6348681: ends in 1 (odd) → fails.

 

• 7699504: even; digit sum = 7+6+9+9+5+0+4 = 40, not divisible by 3 → fails.

 

• 7132950: even; digit sum = 7+1+3+2+9+5+0 = 27, divisible by 3 → divisible by 6 ✓.

 

• 7993043: ends in 3 (odd) → fails.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Eliminate odd numbers first (instant fail for divisibility by 2), then apply the digit-sum test for 3 only on the remaining even numbers.

 

NOTE

 

• Digit-sum test for 3: add all digits; if that sum (or its further digit sum) is divisible by 3, so is the original number.

question: DMART is offering 'Buy 30, get 21 free' on grocery items. What is the net percentage discount being offered by the DMART? (Corrected up to two decimal places)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 41.18%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Scheme: Buy 30 items (pay for 30), get 21 extra items free — total 51 items for the price of 30.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Net discount % = [Free items ÷ (Paid items + Free items)] × 100 = 21 ÷ (30 + 21) × 100 = 21/51 × 100.

 

• 21/51 × 100 = 41.176...% ≈ 41.18%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For 'Buy X, get Y free' schemes, discount % = [Y/(X+Y)] × 100 directly — a ready formula, no need to assume a price.

 

NOTE

 

• The options as printed in this booklet have their leading digits hidden by a printing/overlay glitch (reproduced here exactly as printed); Option A genuinely reads '41.18%'.

question: Two numbers add up to 98. If twice the smaller number minus the bigger number equals 28, find the smaller number.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 42.

 

GIVEN

 

• Smaller (x) + Bigger (y) = 98; 2x − y = 28.

 

SOLUTION

 

• From the sum: y = 98 − x.

 

• Substitute into the second condition: 2x − (98 − x) = 28 ⟹ 3x − 98 = 28 ⟹ 3x = 126 ⟹ x = 42.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Express the bigger number in terms of the smaller (using the sum condition) and substitute immediately — reduces the problem to one simple linear equation.

 

NOTE

 

• Verify: bigger = 98 − 42 = 56; 2(42) − 56 = 84 − 56 = 28 ✓.

question: The sum of ages of three brothers is 52 years. The eldest is 4 years older than the middle brother, and the middle brother is 6 years older than the youngest. Find the age of the eldest brother.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 22 years.

 

GIVEN

 

• Sum of ages of 3 brothers = 52 years. Eldest = Middle + 4; Middle = Youngest + 6.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let youngest = y. Then middle = y + 6, and eldest = (y + 6) + 4 = y + 10.

 

• Sum: y + (y + 6) + (y + 10) = 52 ⟹ 3y + 16 = 52 ⟹ 3y = 36 ⟹ y = 12.

 

• Eldest = y + 10 = 12 + 10 = 22 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Express every unknown age in terms of a single anchor variable (here, the youngest) before summing — avoids handling three separate variables.

 

NOTE

 

• Middle = 12+6=18, Eldest = 18+4=22; check: 12+18+22 = 52 ✓.

question: Isha buys a gold ring for her mother. The gold ring is marked at ₹50,000, and two successive discounts of 30% and R%, respectively, are given. After getting the two successive discounts, she paid ₹14,000. Find the value of R.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 60.

 

GIVEN

 

• Marked price = ₹50,000; successive discounts of 30% and R%; final price paid = ₹14,000.

 

SOLUTION

 

• After the first (30%) discount: 50,000 × 0.7 = ₹35,000.

 

• After the second (R%) discount: 35,000 × (1 − R/100) = 14,000.

 

• (1 − R/100) = 14000/35000 = 0.4 ⟹ R/100 = 0.6 ⟹ R = 60.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Apply successive discounts as successive multiplying factors (1 − discount/100), and solve for the unknown factor last, working step by step.

 

NOTE

 

• Successive discounts are NOT simply additive (30% + R% ≠ total discount) — each discount applies to the already-reduced price.

question: The population of a village increased by 5% in 2023 and was expected to increase again by 6% in 2024. Find the overall percentage increase in the population of the village over the two years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 11.3%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Two successive percentage increases: 5% (2023) and 6% (2024).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Successive % change formula: Net% = a + b + (ab/100), where a and b are the two percentage changes.

 

• Net% = 5 + 6 + (5 × 6)/100 = 11 + 0.3 = 11.3%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Memorise the successive-percentage-change formula Net% = a + b + ab/100 (use a negative sign for any decrease) — avoids assuming a base value and computing twice.

 

NOTE

 

• The options as printed in this booklet have their leading digits hidden by the same printing/overlay glitch seen elsewhere in this paper (reproduced here exactly as printed); Option A genuinely reads '11.3%'.

question: A regular hexagonal tile has a side length of 6 cm. The tile is divided into 6 equilateral triangles by drawing lines from the centre to each vertex. If 3 alternate triangles are painted blue, what is the total blue painted area (rounded off to two decimal places)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 46.77 cm².

 

GIVEN

 

• Regular hexagon, side a = 6 cm, divided into 6 equilateral triangles from the centre; 3 alternate triangles are painted blue.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Area of a regular hexagon = (3√3/2) × a² = (3√3/2) × 36 = 54√3 ≈ 93.53 cm².

 

• Since the hexagon is made of 6 equal triangles and exactly 3 (half) are painted, painted area = 54√3 / 2 = 27√3.

 

• 27√3 ≈ 27 × 1.7320508 ≈ 46.77 cm².

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• A regular hexagon = 6 identical equilateral triangles of the same side; area of each triangle = (√3/4)a² = (√3/4)(36) ≈ 15.59 cm²; multiply by 3 (triangles painted) = 46.77 cm².

 

NOTE

 

• The options as printed in this booklet have their leading digits hidden by the same printing/overlay glitch seen elsewhere in this paper (reproduced here exactly as printed); Option A genuinely reads '46.77 cm²'.

question: If 5^(u+v) = 625 and 625^(u-v) = 5, then the value of u is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 17/8.

 

GIVEN

 

• 5^(u+v) = 625, and 625^(u−v) = 5.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Express 625 as a power of 5: 625 = 5⁴.

 

• From the first equation: 5^(u+v) = 5⁴ ⟹ u + v = 4.

 

• From the second equation: (5⁴)^(u−v) = 5¹ ⟹ 4(u − v) = 1 ⟹ u − v = 1/4.

 

• Adding the two results: 2u = 4 + 1/4 = 17/4 ⟹ u = 17/8.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert every term to the same base (here, base 5) first — this turns a tricky exponential equation into two simple linear equations in u and v.

 

NOTE

 

• Be careful with the direction: from 625^(u−v)=5, we get u − v = 1/4 (a fraction), not 4 — a common slip when the base/exponent are swapped.

question:
If 'E' stands for '+', 'F' stands for '-', 'G' stands for '×' and 'H' stands for '÷', what will come in place of question mark '?' in the following equation?

96 H 12 G 2 E 15 F 9 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 22.

 

GIVEN

 

• E = +, F = −, G = ×, H = ÷.

 

• Expression: 96 H 12 G 2 E 15 F 9 = ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Substitute the actual symbols: 96 ÷ 12 × 2 + 15 − 9.

 

• Division and multiplication share equal priority, so solve strictly left to right: 96 ÷ 12 = 8; 8 × 2 = 16.

 

• Then addition/subtraction left to right: 16 + 15 = 31; 31 − 9 = 22.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• First replace all coded letters with their real symbols, THEN apply BODMAS on the resulting expression as a whole — never calculate symbol by symbol as you decode.

 

NOTE

 

• Division and multiplication rank equally in BODMAS — always resolve them strictly left to right, not 'division always before multiplication'.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements: All ostriches are eagles. No ostrich is a peacock.

Conclusion (I): No eagle is a peacock.

Conclusion (II): Some peacocks are ostriches.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• All ostriches (A) are eagles (B) — a universal affirmative.

 

• No ostrich (A) is a peacock (C) — a universal negative.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Draw the 'possible' Venn diagram: circle A (ostrich) entirely inside circle B (eagle); circle A entirely outside circle C (peacock). But circle C's relation to the rest of circle B (the part of eagles that are NOT ostriches) is completely undefined.

 

• Conclusion (I), 'No eagle is a peacock', is NOT forced — some eagles outside the ostrich-circle could still overlap with peacocks in a valid diagram, so it does not necessarily follow.

 

• Conclusion (II), 'Some peacocks are ostriches', directly contradicts the given premise 'No ostrich is a peacock' — it can never follow.

 

• Since neither is guaranteed true in every possible diagram, neither conclusion follows.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• A universal negative statement ('No A is C') can never validly produce a particular affirmative conclusion about the same terms ('Some C are A') — this instantly rules out such conclusions.

 

NOTE

 

• Always test the 'worst case' (most extreme, still-valid) Venn diagram to check if a conclusion is truly forced — if you can draw even one valid diagram where the conclusion fails, it does not follow.

question: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster DOES NOT belong to that group? (Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. KOO.

 

GIVEN

 

• Clusters: ILM, WZA, TWX, KOO.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert letters to their alphabet positions and check the gap pattern within each cluster.

 

• ILM: I(9) → L(12) is +3, L → M(13) is +1.

 

• WZA: W(23) → Z(26) is +3, Z → A(27, wrapping) is +1.

 

• TWX: T(20) → W(23) is +3, W → X(24) is +1.

 

• KOO: K(11) → O(15) is +4, O → O(15) is +0 — this breaks the shared +3, +1 pattern.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert every cluster to numbers and compare the gap-pattern between consecutive letters — the odd one always breaks the shared step sequence.

 

NOTE

 

• Remember the alphabet wraps around: after Z (26) comes A (1), i.e., Z + 1 = A (or 27, before reducing mod 26).

question: TP 16 is related to LH 8 in a certain way. In the same way, PL 18 is related to HD 9. To which of the given options is LH 12 related, following the same logic?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. DZ 6.

 

GIVEN

 

• TP 16 → LH 8, and PL 18 → HD 9.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check the letter shift: T(20) → L(12) is −8; P(16) → H(8) is −8. And the number: 16 → 8 is halved (÷2).

 

• Confirm with the second pair: P(16) → H(8) is −8; L(12) → D(4) is −8; 18 → 9 is halved. Pattern confirmed: each letter shifts back by 8 (mod 26), and the number is halved.

 

• Apply to LH 12: L(12) − 8 = 4 = D; H(8) − 8 = 0, which wraps around to 26 = Z; number: 12 ÷ 2 = 6.

 

• Result: DZ 6.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Derive the rule from one example, confirm it with the second, then apply it mechanically to the new term.

 

NOTE

 

• When subtracting from H(8): 8 − 8 = 0, which wraps around to Z(26), not to a non-existent '0'.

question:
Refer to the number series given below and answer the question that follows. Counting to be done from left to right only. (NOTE: All numbers are single-digit numbers only.)

(Left) 4 1 8 7 1 5 3 4 2 9 7 3 9 1 9 4 4 9 2 9 2 9 8 1 4 9 (Right)

How many such odd numbers are there each of which is immediately preceded by an odd number and also immediately followed by an even number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 2.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 4 1 8 7 1 5 3 4 2 9 7 3 9 1 9 4 4 9 2 9 2 9 8 1 4 9.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Scan every interior digit for the pattern: odd digit, preceded by an odd digit, followed by an even digit.

 

• '…5, 3, 4…': digit 3 is odd, preceded by 5 (odd) ✓, followed by 4 (even) ✓ — qualifies.

 

• '…1, 9, 4…': digit 9 is odd, preceded by 1 (odd) ✓, followed by 4 (even) ✓ — qualifies.

 

• No other position satisfies all three conditions together — total count = 2.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Mark the parity (Odd/Even) of every digit above the series first, then simply scan for the three-term pattern O-O-E.

 

NOTE

 

• Never count the very first or last digit of the series — they don't have both a preceding and a following neighbour.

question: Sahana starts from Point A and drives 6 km towards west. She then takes a left turn, drives 8 km, turns left and drives 2 km. She then takes a left turn again and drives 4 km. She takes a final right turn, drives 4 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should she drive in order to reach Point A again? (Note: All turns are 90° turns only unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 4 km towards north.

 

GIVEN

 

• A(0,0) → 6 km west → left turn, 8 km → left turn, 2 km → left turn, 4 km → right turn, 4 km → stop at P.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Plot each leg on a coordinate grid: A(0,0) → west 6 → (−6, 0), facing west.

 

• Left turn from west → facing south; drive 8 km south → (−6, −8).

 

• Left turn from south → facing east; drive 2 km east → (−4, −8).

 

• Left turn from east → facing north; drive 4 km north → (−4, −4).

 

• Right turn from north → facing east; drive 4 km east → (0, −4) = P.

 

• Vector from P(0,−4) to A(0,0) = (0, +4), i.e. 4 km towards north.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Plot the path step by step on a rough compass grid with coordinates — far more reliable than mentally tracking turns and directions.

 

NOTE

 

• Always re-derive the new facing direction fresh at each turn (a left turn while facing west leads to facing south) — don't guess based on 'left = north' shortcuts.

question: In a certain code language, 'soup hat honey' is coded as 'vc iw dp' and 'honey wall yak' is coded as 'ar hw iw'. How is 'honey' coded in the given language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. iw.

 

GIVEN

 

• 'soup hat honey' → 'vc iw dp'.

 

• 'honey wall yak' → 'ar hw iw'.

 

SOLUTION

 

• The word common to both given phrases is 'honey'.

 

• The code common to both given coded phrases is 'iw'.

 

• Therefore, honey = iw.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In coded-language questions with two overlapping sentences, always find the ONE common word and the ONE common code — that pairing directly answers 'how is X coded'.

 

NOTE

 

• Don't assume the order of words matches the order of codes; rely only on identifying the common element between both sentences.

question: Seven boxes B, C, D, I, J, K and L are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the same order. Only two boxes are kept between J and B. Only K is kept above I. Only two boxes are kept between K and J. C is kept at some place below L but at some place above D. How many boxes are kept between C and L?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. One.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 boxes stacked: B, C, D, I, J, K, L.

 

• 'Only K is kept above I' ⟹ K is directly above I, with K at the very top.

 

• 'Only two boxes between K and J' ⟹ J is 2 boxes below K.

 

• 'Only two boxes between J and B' ⟹ B is 2 boxes below (or above) J.

 

• C is below L but above D.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Only K is above I' fixes K at position 1 (top) and I at position 2.

 

• 'Only two boxes between K(1) and J' places J at position 4 (positions 2, 3 lie between).

 

• 'Only two boxes between J(4) and B' places B at position 7 (bottom), since position 1 is already taken.

 

• Remaining positions {3, 5, 6} go to L, C, D with the order L (below) → C → D (further below): so L = 3, C = 5, D = 6.

 

• Final order (top to bottom): K, I, L, J, C, D, B.

 

• Between C (position 5) and L (position 3): only J (position 4) lies in between — 1 box.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always place the boxes tied to 'only one/only X' clues first — they anchor the entire stack (here, K is forced to the very top).

 

NOTE

 

• 'Only K is kept above I' is a very strong clue — it means K is not just somewhere above I, but the single box directly above I, at the topmost position.

question:
Refer to the following series and answer the question (all numbers are single digit numbers only). Counting to be done from left to right only.

(Left) 5 7 9 4 2 1 4 7 9 3 2 6 8 5 4 1 9 5 4 3 2 (Right)
