How many such even digits are there each of which is immediately preceded by an even digit and also immediately followed by an even digit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 1.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 5 7 9 4 2 1 4 7 9 3 2 6 8 5 4 1 9 5 4 3 2.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Scan for the pattern: even digit, preceded by even, followed by even (i.e., three consecutive even digits, and we count the middle one).

 

• The only qualifying run is '…2, 6, 8…': digit 6 is even, preceded by 2 (even) ✓, followed by 8 (even) ✓.

 

• No other run of three consecutive even digits exists in the series — total count = 1.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Mark the parity of every digit first, then look only for runs of 3 or more consecutive even digits — a run of length n gives exactly (n − 2) qualifying middle digits.

 

NOTE

 

• Two consecutive evens surrounded by odd digits never qualify — you specifically need at least three evens in a row.

question:
Which of the following letter-number clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete?

7P25 10Q20 ? 16S10 19T5
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 13R15.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series of clusters: 7P25, 10Q20, ?, 16S10, 19T5.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Numbers before the letter: 7, 10, ?, 16, 19 — increasing by 3 each time, so missing = 13.

 

• Letters: P, Q, ?, S, T — consecutive alphabets, so missing = R.

 

• Numbers after the letter: 25, 20, ?, 10, 5 — decreasing by 5 each time, so missing = 15.

 

• Combined missing cluster = 13R15.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Split a complex cluster series into 3 independent, simpler series (before-number, letter, after-number) and solve each one separately.

 

NOTE

 

• The letters run in a simple consecutive sequence (P, Q, R, S, T) — easy to overlook when focused mainly on the numeric patterns.

question: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster DOES NOT belong to that group? (Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. DHI.

 

GIVEN

 

• Clusters: KNP, UXZ, DHI, EHJ.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert to alphabet positions and check the gap pattern: KNP: K(11)→N(14) is +3, N→P(16) is +2.

 

• UXZ: U(21)→X(24) is +3, X→Z(26) is +2.

 

• EHJ: E(5)→H(8) is +3, H→J(10) is +2. All three follow +3, +2.

 

• DHI: D(4)→H(8) is +4, H→I(9) is +1 — breaks the shared pattern.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert letters to numbers and compare the step-differences within each cluster — the odd one always deviates from the shared step pattern.

 

NOTE

 

• Three clusters sharing an identical step-pattern (here +3, +2) while one differs is the standard 'odd one out' structure — always test the numeric gaps, not the visual 'shape' of the letters.

question: A, B, C, R, S, T and U are sitting around a circular table facing the centre of the table. A sits third to the left of R. B sits second to the left of C. R is the immediate neighbour of both U and B. T is not an immediate neighbour of A. How many people sit between S and B when counted from the right of S?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. Two.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people: A, B, C, R, S, T, U, facing the centre. A is 3rd to the left of R; B is 2nd to the left of C; R is the immediate neighbour of both U and B; T is not a neighbour of A.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Fix R at a reference seat (position 0, clockwise numbering, since 'left' when facing the centre corresponds to the clockwise direction).

 

• A is 3rd to the left of R ⟹ A is at position 3.

 

• R's neighbours are positions 6 and 1; these must be {U, B} in some order. Testing B = position 6 (with U = 1) is the arrangement consistent with all clues (B = position 1 leads to a contradiction with B's relation to C).

 

• B = 2nd to the left of C ⟹ C is at position 4 (B − 2).

 

• Remaining positions {2, 5} go to S and T. Since T is NOT a neighbour of A (positions 2, 4 are A's neighbours), T cannot be at position 2, so T = 5 and S = 2.

 

• Final order (clockwise): 0=R, 1=U, 2=S, 3=A, 4=C, 5=T, 6=B.

 

• Counting from the right of S (position 2), i.e. moving counter-clockwise: position 1 (U), position 0 (R), then position 6 (B). People between S and B on this path: U and R — 2 people.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Fix one person as a reference (0°) first, then place everyone else using the 'X to the left/right of Y' clues as direct seat-counts from that reference.

 

NOTE

 

• For people facing the centre, 'left' corresponds to the clockwise direction and 'right' to counter-clockwise around the table — fix this convention before starting.

question: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. B sits second to the right of D. C is the immediate neighbour of A and B. E sits to the immediate right of G. How many people sit between F and B when counted from the left of F?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Five.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people: A, B, C, D, E, F, G, facing the centre. B is 2nd to the right of D; C is the immediate neighbour of both A and B; E sits immediately right of G.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Fix D at position 0. B is 2nd to the right of D (right = counter-clockwise) ⟹ B is at position 5.

 

• C is a neighbour of B, so C is at position 4 or 6. Testing C = 4: C's other neighbour is position 3, which must then be A (the other person C is a neighbour of) ⟹ A = 3.

 

• Remaining positions {1, 2, 6} go to E, F, G, with E immediately right (counter-clockwise) of G, i.e. E = G − 1. Only (G=2, E=1) fits within the remaining set, leaving F = 6.

 

• Final order (clockwise): 0=D, 1=E, 2=G, 3=A, 4=C, 5=B, 6=F.

 

• F (position 6) and B (position 5) are actually adjacent (only 1 step apart, going counter-clockwise/'right'). So going 'from the left of F' means taking the LONG way around: F(6) → 0(D) → 1(E) → 2(G) → 3(A) → 4(C) → 5(B) — passing all 5 other people.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When a question specifies a direction ('from the left of F'), always check whether it's asking for the short way or the long way around the circle — the two paths give complementary counts.

 

NOTE

 

• Self-check: for a 7-person circular table, (people counted via one path) + (people counted via the other path) = total people − 2. Here 5 + 0 = 5 = 7 − 2, since F and B are adjacent via the short path.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

1 1 2 6 24 120 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 720.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 1, 1, 2, 6, 24, 120, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Recognise the factorial series: 0! = 1, 1! = 1, 2! = 2, 3! = 6, 4! = 24, 5! = 120, 6! = 720.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Alternatively spot it via multiplying-factor pattern: term(n) = term(n−1) × n, i.e. the multipliers are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 — so next term = 120 × 6 = 720.

 

NOTE

 

• Factorial series (0! through 7! = 1, 1, 2, 6, 24, 120, 720, 5040) is a very common number-series base in RRB exams — worth memorising.

question:
Refer to the number series given below and answer the question that follows. Counting to be done from left to right only. (NOTE: All numbers are single-digit numbers only.)

(Left) 3 1 6 9 6 2 1 5 8 5 3 3 8 2 6 1 7 3 7 8 7 4 9 1 5 7 4 (Right)

How many such even digits are there, each of which is immediately preceded by an even digit and also immediately followed by an even digit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. One.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 3 1 6 9 6 2 1 5 8 5 3 3 8 2 6 1 7 3 7 8 7 4 9 1 5 7 4.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Scan for runs of three consecutive even digits (needed for a qualifying middle even digit).

 

• The only qualifying run is '…8, 2, 6…': digit 2 is even, preceded by 8 (even) ✓, followed by 6 (even) ✓.

 

• No other run of three consecutive evens exists — total count = 1.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Mark parities first, then scan specifically for runs of 3+ consecutive even digits.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Immediately preceded/followed' means the very next digit, not merely 'nearby' — always check the direct neighbours only.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements: All figs are bananas. All cups are bananas.

Conclusions: (I) Some figs are cups. (II) All cups are figs.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• All figs (A) are bananas (C); All cups (B) are bananas (C) — two universal affirmatives sharing the same predicate.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Both figs and cups are subsets of bananas, but their relationship to EACH OTHER is completely undefined — they could be identical circles, partially overlapping circles, or entirely separate (disjoint) circles, all while still fitting inside the banana circle.

 

• Since a valid diagram exists where figs and cups don't overlap at all, Conclusion (I) 'Some figs are cups' is not guaranteed.

 

• Since a valid diagram exists where cups and figs are not identical, Conclusion (II) 'All cups are figs' is also not guaranteed.

 

• Hence, neither conclusion follows.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 'All A are C, All B are C' NEVER yields any definite relationship between A and B — memorise this as a standard trap pattern.

 

NOTE

 

• Draw the 'worst case' Venn diagram (figs and cups as two separate, non-overlapping circles, both inside bananas) to disprove both conclusions at once.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

1 9 25 ? 81
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 49.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 1, 9, 25, ?, 81.

 

SOLUTION

 

• These are squares of consecutive odd numbers: 1², 3², 5², ?, 9² = 1, 9, 25, ?, 81.

 

• The missing term is 7² = 49.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Learn to instantly recognise common perfect squares (1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 100, 121…) — series based on squares are very common.

 

NOTE

 

• Alternative check via differences: 9−1=8, 25−9=16, ?−25=24 (so ?=49), 81−49=32 — the differences themselves increase by 8 each time.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

87 75 63 51 39 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 27.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 87, 75, 63, 51, 39, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Common difference: 87−75=12; 75−63=12; 63−51=12; 51−39=12 — a constant difference of −12.

 

• Next term = 39 − 12 = 27.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Check the first difference between terms; if it's constant, it's a simple arithmetic progression — just subtract (or add) once more.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify the constant difference across at least 3 consecutive pairs before trusting the pattern.

question: Each of the digits in the number 2365987 is arranged in descending order from right to left. Calculate the sum of the digits whose position(s) remain(s) unchanged as compared to that in the original number.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 13.

 

GIVEN

 

• Original number: 2365987. Rearranging digits so they are in descending order when read right to left (equivalently, ascending order when read left to right).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Original (position 1 to 7, left to right): 2, 3, 6, 5, 9, 8, 7.

 

• Rearranged in ascending order (left to right): 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.

 

• Compare position by position: pos1: 2=2 ✓; pos2: 3=3 ✓; pos3: 6≠5; pos4: 5≠6; pos5: 9≠7; pos6: 8=8 ✓; pos7: 7≠9.

 

• Unchanged positions have digits 2, 3, 8. Sum = 2 + 3 + 8 = 13.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Write the original and the rearranged number one directly below the other, and simply tick off the columns where the digit matches — this visual method avoids mental mix-ups.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Descending order from right to left' is the same as 'ascending order from left to right' — translate the phrasing carefully before sorting the digits.

question: DI 2 is related to UZ 8 in a certain way. In the same way, MR 4 is related to DI 64. To which of the given options is OT 3 related, following the same logic?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. FK 27.

 

GIVEN

 

• DI 2 → UZ 8, and MR 4 → DI 64.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check the letter shift: D(4)+17=21=U ✓; I(9)+17=26=Z ✓. Confirm with the second pair: M(13)+17=30, mod 26 = 4 = D ✓; R(18)+17=35, mod 26 = 9 = I ✓. So each letter shifts by +17 (mod 26).

 

• Check the number: 2³=8 ✓, and 4³=64 ✓ — the number is cubed.

 

• Apply to OT 3: O(15)+17=32, mod 26 = 6 = F; T(20)+17=37, mod 26 = 11 = K; number: 3³ = 27.

 

• Result: FK 27.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For letter analogies, compute the position-shift on both given example pairs first; a consistent shift confirms the rule. For numbers, test simple operations (square, cube, ×constant) against the given pair.

 

NOTE

 

• A shift of +17 is the same as a shift of −9 (since 17 = 26 − 9) — use whichever direction is quicker to compute mentally.

question: In a certain code language, 'desk round mom' is coded as 'md ei wx' and 'mom wheat bell' is coded as 'um ac ei'. How is 'mom' coded in the given language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. ei.

 

GIVEN

 

• 'desk round mom' → 'md ei wx'.

 

• 'mom wheat bell' → 'um ac ei'.

 

SOLUTION

 

• The word common to both phrases is 'mom'.

 

• The code common to both coded phrases is 'ei'.

 

• Therefore, mom = ei.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Same 'common word ⟺ common code' method used in similar questions — always identify the overlapping word between the two given sentences first.

 

NOTE

 

• 'ei' is the only code shared between both coded sentences, confirming the match uniquely.

question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

(13, 39, 3)

(15, 75, 5)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. (12, 36, 3).

 

GIVEN

 

• Pattern sets: (13, 39, 3) and (15, 75, 5).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Test the relation: 13 × 3 = 39 ✓ (matches the middle number). 15 × 5 = 75 ✓ (matches too). So, Middle number = First number × Third number.

 

• Check each option: (5,25,15): 5×15=75≠25 ✗. (64,8,4): 64×4=256≠8 ✗. (10,35,3): 10×3=30≠35 ✗. (12,36,3): 12×3=36=36 ✓.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Once you spot the rule (middle = first × third) from the two given sets, just test each option's first and third numbers against its middle number.

 

NOTE

 

• The question explicitly disallows digit-breaking tricks — always look for a whole-number arithmetic operation (like multiplication here) first.

question: RBUL is related to VXYH in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, ZTCD is related to DPGZ. To which of the given options is HLKV related, following the same logic?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. LHOR.

 

GIVEN

 

• RBUL → VXYH, and ZTCD → DPGZ.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check the letter shift for each position: R(+4)=V ✓; B(−4)=X ✓ (2−4=−2, mod 26 = 24 = X); U(+4)=Y ✓; L(−4)=H ✓. So odd positions (1st, 3rd) shift +4, even positions (2nd, 4th) shift −4.

 

• Confirm with the second pair: Z(+4)=D(mod 26) ✓; T(−4)=P ✓; C(+4)=G ✓; D(−4)=Z(mod 26) ✓ — gives DPGZ, matching exactly.

 

• Apply to HLKV: H(8)+4=12=L; L(12)−4=8=H; K(11)+4=15=O; V(22)−4=18=R.

 

• Result: LHOR.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Write position numbers under each letter of both example words, spot the alternating +4/−4 pattern, then apply it directly to the new word.

 

NOTE

 

• Watch for the mod-26 wraparound whenever a shift crosses past A or Z (e.g., D(4)−4=0, which wraps to Z=26).

question: In a certain code language, P # Q means 'P is the father of Q', P % Q means 'P is the sister of Q', P @ Q means 'P is the wife of Q' and P & Q means 'P is the brother of Q'. Based on the above, how is G related to J if 'G @ D # B @ K # J'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. Mother's mother.

 

GIVEN

 

• G @ D # B @ K # J, where @ = wife of, # = father of.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Break the chain: G@D means G is the wife of D. D#B means D is the father of B. B@K means B is the wife of K. K#J means K is the father of J.

 

• Since D is B's father and G is D's wife, G is B's mother.

 

• Since K is J's father and B is K's wife, B is J's mother.

 

• So G is the mother of B, who is the mother of J — meaning G is J's maternal grandmother, i.e. 'Mother's mother'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Decode a family-code chain strictly left to right, one symbol at a time, sketching a quick family tree — never try to solve it all mentally in one leap.

 

NOTE

 

• The symbol '@' (wife of) directly reveals gender — the person before '@' is always female — use this to avoid gender-assumption mistakes further down the chain.

question: Juhi starts from point A and drives 57 km towards the North. She then takes a right turn, drives 58 km, turns right and drives 61 km. She then takes a right turn and drives 60 km. She takes a final right turn, drives 4 km and stops at point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should she drive in order to reach point A again? (All turns are 90 degrees turns only unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 2 km to the east.

 

GIVEN

 

• A(0,0) → 57 km north → right turn, 58 km → right turn, 61 km → right turn, 60 km → right turn, 4 km → stop at P.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Plot on a grid: A(0,0) → north 57 → (0, 57), facing north.

 

• Right turn from north → facing east; drive 58 km east → (58, 57).

 

• Right turn from east → facing south; drive 61 km south → (58, −4).

 

• Right turn from south → facing west; drive 60 km west → (−2, −4).

 

• Right turn from west → facing north; drive 4 km north → (−2, 0) = P.

 

• Vector from P(−2, 0) to A(0, 0) = (+2, 0), i.e. 2 km towards the east.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Net north-south displacement = 57 − 61 + 4 = 0; net east-west displacement = 58 − 60 = −2 (i.e., 2 km west of A), so the return path is 2 km east.

 

NOTE

 

• With four successive 90° right turns, directions cycle N → E → S → W → N — plotting coordinates avoids direction-confusion.

question:
If + means −, − means ×, × means ÷ and ÷ means +, then what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

131 − 7 ÷ 32 + 362 × 2 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 768.

 

GIVEN

 

• Printed '+' actually means '−'; printed '−' means '×'; printed '×' means '÷'; printed '÷' means '+'.

 

• Expression: 131 − 7 ÷ 32 + 362 × 2.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Rewrite the expression with its TRUE operations: 131 × 7 + 32 − 362 ÷ 2.

 

• Apply BODMAS on this rewritten expression: 362 ÷ 2 = 181; 131 × 7 = 917.

 

• 917 + 32 − 181 = 949 − 181 = 768.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Rewrite the ENTIRE expression with the true operations first, then solve it fresh using standard BODMAS — never calculate symbol-by-symbol while decoding, as that invites errors.

 

NOTE

 

• BODMAS applies to the REPLACED (true) expression, not to the originally printed symbols.

question:
This question is based on the five, three-digit numbers given below.

(Left) 582 128 563 183 592 (Right)

(Example- 697 – First digit = 6, second digit = 9 and third digit = 7)

NOTE - All operations to be done from left to right.

What will be the resultant if the third digit of the highest number is added to the second digit of the lowest number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 4.

 

GIVEN

 

• Numbers: 582, 128, 563, 183, 592.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Highest number = 592; its third digit = 2.

 

• Lowest number = 128; its second digit = 2.

 

• Required sum = 2 + 2 = 4.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• First identify the highest and lowest numbers by simple comparison, then read off only the required digit positions — no need to examine the other three numbers at all.

 

NOTE

 

• 'First/second/third digit' is always counted from the left, exactly as shown in the example given in the question.

question: Seven boxes B, C, D, I, J, K and L are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the same order. Only I is kept above L. Only three boxes are kept between I and B. Only K is kept below C. D is kept immediately above B. How many boxes are kept between J and K?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Three.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 boxes stacked: B, C, D, I, J, K, L.

 

• 'Only I is kept above L' ⟹ I is directly above L, with I at the very top.

 

• 'Only three boxes between I and B' ⟹ B is 4 boxes below I.

 

• 'Only K is kept below C' ⟹ K is directly below C, with K at the very bottom.

 

• 'D is kept immediately above B'.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Only I is above L' fixes I at position 1 (top) and L at position 2.

 

• 'Only three boxes between I(1) and B' places B at position 5 (positions 2, 3, 4 lie between).

 

• 'Only K is below C, with K at the very bottom' places K at position 7 and C at position 6.

 

• 'D is immediately above B(5)' places D at position 4.

 

• The one remaining position, 3, goes to J (the only box left).

 

• Final order (top to bottom): I, L, J, D, B, C, K.

 

• Between J (position 3) and K (position 7): D, B, C lie in between — 3 boxes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Fix the boxes tied to 'only one' clues first (I at the very top, K at the very bottom) — they anchor the whole stack before you place the rest.

 

NOTE

 

• This is a mirror-style puzzle to a similar 'boxes' question elsewhere in this paper, but with different clue values — always re-derive the arrangement fresh, never reuse a previous answer's positions.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order?

CMN KUV SCD AKL ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. IST.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series of 3-letter clusters: CMN, KUV, SCD, AKL, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• 1st letters: C(3), K(11), S(19), A(1, i.e. 27 before wrap) — each increasing by +8 (mod 26). Next = 27 + 8 = 35, mod 26 = 9 = I.

 

• 2nd letters: M(13), U(21), C(3, i.e. 29), K(11, i.e. 37) — same +8 pattern. Next = 37 + 8 = 45, mod 26 = 19 = S.

 

• 3rd letters: N(14), V(22), D(4, i.e. 30), L(12, i.e. 38) — same +8 pattern. Next = 38 + 8 = 46, mod 26 = 20 = T.

 

• Missing cluster = IST.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Split the cluster series into 3 independent, parallel single-letter series (1st letters, 2nd letters, 3rd letters), and solve each with simple +8 (mod 26) arithmetic.

 

NOTE

 

• Always remember the mod-26 wraparound: after Z (26), the count continues again from A (1).

question: Six cadets, Ram, Shyam, Ravi, John, Noel and Rohan, are standing around a round flag-hoisting pole, facing towards the centre. Noel is the immediate neighbour of Ram and Rohan. John is third to the left of Ram. Ravi and Shyam are sitting next to each other. John is a neighbour of both Shyam and Rohan. Who amongst the following is sitting between Ram and Shyam, when counted from the left of Shyam?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. Ravi.

 

GIVEN

 

• 6 people facing the centre: Ram, Shyam, Ravi, John, Noel, Rohan.

 

• Noel is the immediate neighbour of both Ram and Rohan; John is 3rd to the left of Ram; Ravi and Shyam sit next to each other; John is a neighbour of both Shyam and Rohan.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Fix Ram at position 0. John is 3rd to the left of Ram (left = clockwise) ⟹ John = position 3.

 

• Noel is a neighbour of Ram, so Noel is at position 1 or 5. Testing Noel = 1: Noel's other neighbour (position 2) must be Rohan (since Noel is also Rohan's neighbour) ⟹ Rohan = 2.

 

• Remaining positions {4, 5} go to Ravi and Shyam. John (position 3) is a neighbour of Rohan (position 2, already satisfied) and must also be a neighbour of Shyam, so Shyam = position 4, leaving Ravi = position 5.

 

• Final order (clockwise): 0=Ram, 1=Noel, 2=Rohan, 3=John, 4=Shyam, 5=Ravi.

 

• Counting from the left of Shyam (position 4) towards Ram (position 0), moving clockwise: position 5 (Ravi), then position 0 (Ram). The person in between is Ravi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Place the person from the most restrictive clue ('third to the left/right of X') relative to a fixed reference first — it narrows down possibilities fastest.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Immediate neighbour of both X and Y' always means the person sits directly between X and Y — treat such clues as a fixed 3-person block.

question: Which technology was used in 2025 to create the latest lab-grown human lung microtissues?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3D bioprinting with stem cells.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 2025, scientists used 3D bioprinting technology combined with stem cells to create lab-grown human lung microtissues, a major step forward in regenerative medicine and respiratory disease research. (3D बायोप्रिंटिंग — स्टेम कोशिकाओं से फेफड़े के ऊतक)

 

• 3D bioprinting builds tissue structures layer-by-layer using 'bio-inks' containing living cells, closely mimicking the natural architecture of organs like the lung's air sacs (alveoli) and airways.

 

• Such lab-grown microtissues are used to study lung diseases (like fibrosis, COPD, and infections), test new drugs without animal or human trials, and work towards future tissue-repair/transplant therapies.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Stem cells are undifferentiated cells capable of developing into many different specialised cell types, making them central to tissue-engineering research.

 

• Organ-on-a-chip and organoid technologies are related approaches used to model human organs in the lab for research purposes.

 

• India has been expanding its biotechnology and regenerative-medicine research capacity through institutions like the Department of Biotechnology (DBT) and various IITs/AIIMS.

 

NOTE

 

• Quantum protein folding simulation (Option A): A computational technique for predicting protein structures, not a tissue-fabrication method.

 

• CRISPR editing (Option C): A gene-editing tool used to modify DNA sequences, distinct from the tissue-fabrication (bioprinting) technique used here.

 

• AI-driven organoid modeling (Option D): Refers to using AI to analyse/model organoids, not the direct fabrication technique (bioprinting) used to build the microtissue itself.

question: Which of the following institutions launched WhatsApp Channel for verified financial updates in April 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Reserve Bank of India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) launched an official WhatsApp Channel in April 2025 to share verified financial updates, press releases and public notices directly with citizens, aiming to combat misinformation and fraud in the name of the central bank. (भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक — व्हाट्सएप चैनल, अप्रैल 2025)

 

• This move is part of RBI's broader financial literacy and consumer-protection push, ensuring the public receives authentic information straight from the source.

 

• RBI is India's central banking institution, responsible for regulating the monetary policy and the banking system of the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and was nationalised in 1949; its headquarters is in Mumbai.

 

• The Governor of RBI (as of the exam period) is Sanjay Malhotra.

question: Which agency launched 'Bharatpol' in January 2025, to streamline real-time Interpol communication for Indian agencies?

The correct answer is Central Bureau of Investigation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), India's nodal agency for Interpol coordination, launched the 'Bharatpol' portal in January 2025 to streamline and speed up real-time communication between Indian law-enforcement agencies and Interpol. (भारतपोल — CBI, जनवरी 2025)

 

• Bharatpol enables State and Central law-enforcement agencies to directly seek Interpol assistance (like Red Corner Notices) through the CBI, without procedural delays, aiding in tracking fugitives and international criminals.

 

• Bharatpol was formally launched by the Union Home Minister at CBI headquarters in New Delhi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• CBI is India's premier investigating agency, functioning under the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT), and also serves as the designated National Central Bureau (NCB) for INTERPOL in India.

 

• INTERPOL (International Criminal Police Organization), headquartered in Lyon, France, facilitates worldwide police cooperation and crime control.

 

• A Red Corner Notice is an Interpol alert requesting law-enforcement worldwide to locate and provisionally arrest a person pending extradition.

 

NOTE

• Reserve Bank of India (Option B): India's central bank, focused on monetary policy and banking regulation.

question: What was India's position in the 2025 Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI)?
solution_text:

• India was ranked 10th in the Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) 2025, continuing to be recognised among the better-performing large economies on climate action. (जलवायु परिवर्तन प्रदर्शन सूचकांक 2025 — भारत की रैंक 10वीं)

 

• The CCPI is published annually by Germanwatch, the NewClimate Institute, and the Climate Action Network (CAN), evaluating countries on GHG emissions, renewable energy, energy use, and climate policy.

question: The IRIS chip developed by the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras and ISRO is based on which indigenous microprocessor architecture?
solution_text:
The correct answer is SHAKTI.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The IRIS chip, developed jointly by IIT Madras and ISRO, is based on the SHAKTI microprocessor architecture — India's indigenous, open-source processor design based on the RISC-V instruction set. (IRIS चिप — शक्ति प्रोसेसर आर्किटेक्चर)

 

• IRIS is a space-grade microprocessor aimed at reducing India's dependence on imported chips for critical applications like satellites and space missions, in line with the Atmanirbhar Bharat (self-reliant India) initiative.

 

• SHAKTI was developed by the RISE (Reconfigurable Intelligent Systems Engineering) Group at IIT Madras, with funding support from the Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• RISC-V is an open-standard instruction set architecture (ISA), free for anyone to use, which has enabled countries like India to design their own indigenous processors without licensing costs.

 

• Other indigenous chip initiatives in India include the VEGA processor series (also from a C-DAC-led effort) and the semiconductor push under the India Semiconductor Mission.

 

• ISRO uses indigenous processors in satellites and launch vehicles to enhance strategic self-reliance and reduce dependency on foreign suppliers.

 

NOTE

 

• Intel x86 (Option A): A proprietary processor architecture developed by Intel, widely used in personal computers — not an indigenous Indian design.

 

• MIPS (Option B): Another (foreign, licensed) processor architecture, unrelated to this indigenous Indian chip effort.

 

• ARM Cortex (Option D): A widely-used processor architecture licensed by the UK-based company Arm, not an Indian indigenous design.

question: Who won the Men's Singles title at the 2025 Australian Open?

question: In May 2025, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) released the Human Development Index (HDI), 2024, report. What was India's rank in the HDI list?

question: As per the Government of India's report in July 2025, which of the following states processed the highest quantity of e-waste during 2024-25?

question: The Indian Prime Minister launched a scheme with a budgetary allocation of ₹11,440 crore for the period 2025-26 to 2030-31 on 11 October 2025, named ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses.

• The mission aims to make India self-reliant (Aatmanirbhar) in pulses production, focusing especially on key crops like tur (arhar), urad and masoor, to reduce India's dependence on pulses imports.

 

• It involves measures like distributing high-yield seeds, promoting better agronomic practices, and ensuring remunerative prices for farmers through procurement support.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

• This mission is part of India's broader push under the Aatmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India) initiative across various sectors including agriculture, defence, and manufacturing.

 

• The scheme complements other agricultural schemes aimed at boosting farmer incomes and crop diversification, such as PM-AASHA (Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay SanraksHan Abhiyan).

 

NOTE

 

• PM Krishi Sinchai Yojana (Option A): A scheme focused on improving irrigation coverage and water-use efficiency in agriculture, launched earlier (2015), unrelated to this 2025 pulses mission.

 

• PM Fasal Bima Yojana (Option B): India's crop insurance scheme (launched 2016), providing insurance coverage against crop failure, distinct from the pulses self-reliance mission.

 

• Mission for Cotton Productivity (Option D): Not the scheme referred to in the question; the actual scheme launched on this date targeted pulses, not cotton.

question: How many years had Narendra Modi completed as Prime Minister of India by May 2025?
